lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Well, it's that time of year again when the annual Pioneer Parade happens in Steinbach. The parade has changed over the years, at least from what I remember it. We don't have the excitement of planning a float and seeing some of the ingenuity of the kids who decorated their bikes or businesses that showed off all their products in a very unique way. But the one thing that hasn't changed is that the parade ends at the Mennonite Heritage Village. August Long Weekend has been the time when we celebrate the heritage of our community. MHV has been part of Steinbach and holds much of the Mennonite history since it was incorporated in 1964. It tells the story of Mennonite settlers to southern Manitoba in a museum complex with over 30 heritage buildings, monuments, permanent and temporary exhibit galleries, and school programs. Each year, over 50,000 visitors from around the world view our 16,000 artifacts, that have been collected. Steinbach teacher, collector of artifacts, and historian John C. Reimer had a deep love of history. As early as 1934, he would bring artifacts of historical interest to his classes in Blumenort. In 1949, he helped form a museum committee to celebrate the 75th anniversary of the first Mennonite migration to Manitoba. In 1951, he purchased his grandfather Kloss R. Reimer's old store, restored it to its original state, and it still exists today at the MHV. And it was Steinbach's first museum. In 1961, a new museum subcommittee purchased 6 acres of land north of Steinbach to build a museum, and later another 34 acres were added to this site. Fundraising for the museum was started by a grant from the town of Steinbach of $50,000. And the city continues to provide granting each year to its operation. Mennonite Heritage Village was officially incorporated in 1964, then built a main building, which today is the auditorium, and that opened its doors to visitors in 1967. A fully operating Dutch windmill was added in 1972. It is similar to the one built in Steinbach in the 1880s. It was rebuilt in 2001 after a fire destroyed the original windmill and stands as the only functioning windmill In Canada today. In the mid-1980s, a new complex was required for the village centre— admin offices, gift shops, space for social functions, rentals, as well as gallery space to tell the story of the expanding museum's artifacts collection. The new village centre, as it stands today, opened in 1989. The museum relies on over 150 dedicated volunteers each year and the service and expertise they bring to the work of the museum, whether tending to the grounds, working special events, area garden club, horse club, or the steel— steam club, or just working one of the buildings as a windmill operator, a blacksmith, printer, or a cook, and others needed during event days. While some things stay the same, Mennonite Heritage Village has changed much since its beginning, and today it continues to expand and build upon the vision of its founders. The province of Manitoba has designated it a signature museum and star attraction. And almost daily during the summer months, visitors to the museum are from outside of the province of Manitoba and outside of Canada. Much credit goes to the vision of its founders, but also to the current and past board members that have continued to make it a tourist destination in Steinbach. Certainly worth seeing, and for, uh, as community members of Steinbach, is worth volunteering at. Thank you, Mr. Mayor.

However, this is the type of building that we're kind of gearing towards providing some opportunities for those that like to go south in winter and have some amenities within their space. Next slide, please. Potential garden plots. This is something I saw at another development in Winnipeg and I've seen them online. We do have several large decks on some of our patios, and people actually use them for, for vegetables and all kinds of different things, flowers, and it's nice to see that. Our vision is to allow room to create some garden plots throughout the property for residents to enjoy. Next slide, please. Again, a potential swimming pool. Obviously, it'd all be fenced in and meet building code and be upkept. To my knowledge, there's only one older apartment in Steinbach that has that, and I always thought that was cool when I was a kid, right by the high school. However, I don't even know if they use it anymore, but I just think it'd be a neat thing to offer people, or even just a couple hot tubs, outdoor patio and stuff. But I won't read all those, but we all know there's lots of benefits of a hot tub and a pool. Thank you. Or even just one or the other for relaxation. And we're all about trying to come up with some ideas that will provide, like I said, a higher quality tenant experience for residents. Next slide, please. Potential guest suite. Again, just potential depending on the feedback that we receive. None of my apartments currently have a guest suite because they're not like a walk-up style with elevator like this building would be. Okay. But many tenants live in a beautiful apartment but don't have enough space for guests to stay overnight. So a guest suite is the answer for that. It can be booked by any tenants for their guests. Residents will love the flexibility to invite out-of-town guests to come visit while residing here. And a potential common amenity room. Again, I've seen a lot of this in Winnipeg. It's not seen here as often, but you could have big screen TV, pool table, kitchenette, lounge furniture, fireplace, things like that would be good for residents and guests to enjoy each other's company without having to necessarily necessarily be inside the resident's home. This builds community and is a great place to have some extra features for residents to enjoy. A potential golf simulator. My boss has one in a shop. It's really cool. And I know there's a lot of guys that like golfing, gals too, of course. And we can only do it for 4 or 5 months a year here. So I think it'd be— I think it'd be a neat idea to make a room that could have that as well as TV for sports and other things. So that's just another option again that I wanna have in one of the next apartment buildings I do to give people kind of a voice and let them kind of vote and see what types of features they'd like to see. A potential coffee bar, I've seen that. Next slide, please. I've seen that in some apartments just to provide a really high-end, high-quality coffee at an affordable price, just so it's kind So kind of a maintenance person would self-serve. They would take care of and refill all this, and people could basically have their coffee at a much reduced price to what the store is on their way out in the morning. Next slide, please. This kind of gives you an idea of the site overview. This is taken from another excerpt of a plan similar to this, but it's slightly different size and had another building, so I just cropped it out just to kind of show you the one building. Thank you. There. Next slide, please. We know there will be opposition on something like this. However, I would just love to share on this one particular site that we did on First Street back in 2019. We bought, I think, 3 of the 6 homes were, were like this. One of them was even boarded up. This one was also boarded up at some point. Thank you. I mean, we believe, yeah, it is a lot more densified to the neighborhood. However, we've built a really nice product there. We have an excellent tenant— I hate to say tenant pool, but tenant base. They're great people. We have good quality people with professional jobs, good jobs, contributing to the community and keeping their places nice. And we believe it's a nice— was a nice addition to that street. Thank you. Which I've said before. Next slide, please. So a few Q&As. I know there's more, but some of the main things are, why is this site suited for multifamily housing? Based on market research and our nearly 0% vacancy at all times in Steinbach and Niverville, the statistics show more than ever that infill densification housing is needed more than ever. We have many applicants for our units that wish we had more units downtown that are close to all amenities. As the members of community will allude to, these older homes we wish to tear down are an eyesore and also don't contribute well to the property tax base for the City of Steinbach and its infrastructure. Question 2 there, will there be drainage issues? Of course there can always be drainage issues, and we are committed to working with both the City of Steinbach and our engineers and your engineers to ensure that we meet the city specifications. We want to always Ensure proper storm management and drainage as required. And, and that's even if we didn't want to, wouldn't be our choice because that's, uh, that's what, uh, you guys pay the big bucks to the people that are supposed to monitor that and make sure that they're— that we're doing our job correctly and that it won't affect others negatively. So we intend to follow those, those requirements. Traffic issues. Given Third Street is a well-designed street to accommodate traffic coming and going from all directions, we believe it is Yes. Is the area suited to handle more infill housing? Yes, it will be slightly busier, obviously, but there are— I don't know what the traffic count is in that area, but there's a lot. I've lived in that area and I've lived in the Steinbach area my whole life, and I don't feel a fear that that would— there'd be more than what it can handle there. Will there be any affordable options? Yes, the development has been designed to accommodate some smaller studio and 1-bedroom style units. That help provide a more affordable option for those looking to downsize, whether to save money or to simplify their lives, but still wanting a high-quality offering at the same time. And location, with this location being close to Fernwood as well as just down the street from the other formerly approved Third Street project, we believe it's consistent with the City of Steinbach's future vision and growth of the downtown core. And being directly— next slide, please. Being directly involved with 200 residential units in the past 5 years, We strive to be leaders in the industry in quality design and resident living experience. We believe that this development would be a great asset to the City of Steinbach. And next slide, please. I look forward to the potential for the development to be offered to our community and ask for your support today as a first step towards seeing this vision become a reality. And that's it. Thanks.

lines.title: Applicant's representative
lines.label: Luke Wiebe (Applicant's representative, Kingdom Home Building Inc.)
lines.text: In light of the situation, through you, Mr. Mayor, to the administration, out of respect for the residents of Steinbach on Third Street area, is it possible that I could ask to table this meeting and come up with a new plan within, say, 2 months that I could go door to door and talk to the community about that would be completely different from this plan? Is that something that's an option? Because it's something I'm willing to consider.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: I'd just like to communicate with administration. Mr. Warkentin, is this something that could happen?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: It is possible if city council wishes to adjourn the public hearing to reconvene at a later date. If that is the case, then council, if it's prepared to If council were to act on the request of Mr. Wiebe, then council would need to determine what the reconvened date of this public hearing would be. And as the original intent of rezoning from RLD to RMD, in my understanding of the request, would be similar, it's just a different proposal within the RMD rezoning. Thank you. That would still be able to be heard under this public hearing process under Bylaw 2231.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Just for clarification, if we do this, we would adjourn the public hearing?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Correct.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: And leave it as it is, and then we would— when we come back to it, we don't have to open the public hearing, we just reconvene?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Yes. However, city council would need to set adjournment. Otherwise, a readvertising process needs to be started from scratch.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. So then the question would be, does council want to go down this road? No.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Comments?

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Yeah, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I would recommend against that. I think that the idea here of a public hearing is that we get the public's input. We get the information and then we make a decision. If the developer has suddenly decided he wants to consult with the neighbourhood, then he's welcome in a year or 2 to come up with an actual— with a plan and consult with the neighbours, and we can have a public hearing at that time. But I don't think tabling it for 2 months in the middle of this here because he suddenly discovered the neighbours have opposition, I just— no. We decide here on this application, and if he wants to try again in the future when it's a If that's allowed under the rules, then go about the way that he's decided he wants to do it.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: I just want to comment. I agree with Councillor Zwaagstra. The due diligence needs to be done before the public hearing, and I also feel it's unfair to the residents to have something like this suspended over 2 months. The decision, whether approval or denial, ultimately should be made today, and that the residents shouldn't have to be suspended and then have to come out again to voice Any concerns at a future public hearing.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Council, I feel there's consensus on this side. Consensus. I believe that. And, you know, I agree completely with Councillor Penner and Councillor Zwaagstra. I think the right thing to do here is to continue. I respect that.

lines.speaker: Luke Wiebe
lines.title: Applicant's representative
lines.label: Luke Wiebe (Applicant's representative, Kingdom Home Building Inc.)
lines.text: Can I just withdraw my application then? Is that not— just to save everybody time? Like, I'd be willing to do that. I don't feel the need to be— it's not that I didn't believe, Mr. Zwaagstra, that people would be opposed to this plan. However, this is— I'm hearing enough. I know that I'm going to hear the same thing, and it's a bit different than some of my other hearings that I've been in, and I'm not asking you— I mean, if everybody wants to speak, that's totally fine. They're all entitled to that, but I'm fine with denying— I'm basically saying I'm fine with us denying the application at this time, even if it means I have to wait another year, and if you're not willing to allow me to come up with a new plan. That's the reason I'm saying that, out of respect for the residents and everyone's time.

lines.speaker: Luke Wiebe
lines.title: Applicant's representative
lines.label: Luke Wiebe (Applicant's representative, Kingdom Home Building Inc.) [medium]
lines.text: They've come all this way and they've spent the time getting ready. Perfect. So yeah, respect for them is at the utmost at this point. Yep.

lines.speaker: Luke Wiebe
lines.title: Applicant's representative
lines.label: Luke Wiebe (Applicant's representative, Kingdom Home Building Inc.)
lines.text: Just wanted to know if it was an option. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: I guess the— should we go into denying then, or—

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Yes, Mr. Mayor. If the applicant If the applicant has requested a withdrawal of his application, then my recommendation would be for council to close the public hearing unless it wishes to hear any more information and then proceed to make a decision at second reading. And if that decision is for the bylaw to be denied, then that would provide clarity to the— to this file as it stands today.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you. Okay, Councillors.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Just a question through you. Does it make a difference if it's documented how many official objections there are? Like, if we go this route, I still think we should formally document the number of objections, even if they don't all speak, but maybe formally submit their objections.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: That will to some degree already be reflected in the minutes that are recorded because this is a public meeting. However, if the request from the applicant is to withdraw and council moves to deny second reading, that's the end of it. The bylaw is dead.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Well, I do— I thank you, everyone, for coming out. and voicing your opinion. And I think at this time, I think it would be wise to save everyone some time. But I do want to thank you. And if you really want to speak, if there's something you want to say, I would keep the podium open for you. But we do, I think I would still like to keep the petition on file with this file, 'cause I think that that needs to come with all the paperwork as well. But at this time, I will close the public hearing, open the council meeting, and then we, I'd like to vote on it. But do you, if you have something, I'd like, yeah, I'd love to hear you. It just, you'll have to go to the podium. Thank you, Mr. Mayor.

lines.speaker: Resident 4
lines.label: Resident 4
lines.text: Thank you. Um, I feel like we were interrupted. Okay, so here's the forum. This is a hearing. This has been expressed to us that we have the right to come before you guys as a council to express our concerns. I appreciate the feedback that you guys have given, um, and And now if we close it, I feel like in midstream he came up and he said something. We—he had his opportunity to share something, and I feel like before the council we have our opportunity to share something. And for you to close it now, I feel like it—there's things that are maybe left unsaid. And so I feel like for our community. I feel like it would be appropriate to continue and to help us or to allow us to be able to have the voice now at this time.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. Okay, even though the project's been pulled, I respect what you're saying and I will let everyone be heard. Thank you very much for speaking. And who would like to go next?

lines.speaker: Resident 8
lines.label: Resident 8
lines.text: Okay. I'm [Resident 8]. In your papers, it would be [Resident 8], living at 121 Lumber. This development, or this whole rezoning, is in our backyard. My husband and I have— I've lived there since 2009, and he has— we just recently got married a few years ago. Um, I just want to say I agree with what has been shared. Um, these are our friends and our neighbors here, and I totally agree. I sent an email to all of you and shared my, my objections to the whole thing, and I still stand on that, and I think even with the redesign of the idea, I don't think that most of us would be in agreement with it either. So that's my objection.

lines.speaker: Resident 9
lines.label: Resident 9
lines.text: Thank you. Me and my husband also disagree with what has been said.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Your name is?

lines.speaker: Resident 9
lines.label: Resident 9
lines.text: [Resident 9]. [Resident 9], 372 Third Street. This would be right in our backyard.

lines.speaker: Resident 9
lines.label: Resident 9
lines.text: We would be afraid of what would be there. It's 10 feet from our property line.

lines.speaker: Resident 9
lines.label: Resident 9
lines.text: And the rentals that are going on there, there's lots of unfriendly things happening. And yeah, so I object.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Resident 10
lines.label: Resident 10
lines.text: Hi, my name is [Resident 10]. I live at 373 Fourth Street. My husband and I have lived there for 25-plus years, and we object to this. It is too big. Thank you. There's too many and it's not the right size. It's not the right fit for the neighbourhood.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Resident 11
lines.label: Resident 11
lines.text: [Resident 11]. We're from 106 Lumber Avenue, me and my wife [name withheld]. And we're just recent to the area. We just moved in this summer. So this was quite a big surprise to us to see that there might be a new development there. And we appreciate the opportunity we've been given to respond and that action is taken in response to it. We're encouraged by the support of the community and excited to be a part of it, to have joined everyone. We also object to the current plan and I don't know. If there's another plan, then we would be interested to see what that would be, if it would be suitable or not. But objection the way it is, at least.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Resident 12
lines.label: Resident 12
lines.text: Hi, my name is [Resident 12], 348 Third Street. I've lived there about 10— almost 10 years. I object to it. It's big, and I suspect that if they light that thing up, like the parking lot and all that, that's going to be a problem too for the people who live nearby there. And I hope if they do come up with a new plan, they take that into account a bit.

lines.speaker: Resident 12
lines.label: Resident 12 [medium]
lines.text: Thank you. I think that's all I have to say right now.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Resident 13
lines.label: Resident 13
lines.text: Hi, my name is [Resident 13] on 117 Lumber. I'm a very, very new addition to the neighbourhood, so hi to everyone who doesn't know me. We just moved in 2 months ago. And I can tell you that in just 2 months of living there, we, my brother and I who live there, We can really feel the sense of community in that neighborhood. We have lovely neighbors and we're welcomed with open arms on every side. It's very wonderful people all around. And I think it's not really a matter of redesign, hot tub, gardens. None of that really matters. The point is that this development just does not fit in this space. I was raised in the La Broquerie Steinbach area my whole life and I actually never knew there was such a nice green space space back there, and it was a lot of the reason why we chose to move here. And so I agree with a lot of what our neighbors have said, that this is just a hidden gem in the community. It would be a really shame to take that away from these families who have lived here. I've heard 25 years, 40-plus years. Someone said houses passed down from one generation to the next. This is a community of people. These are families. There's a lot of love in this neighborhood and in that green space itself. Thank you. Nothing belongs on there other than green space. Thank you. I oppose this project.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Is there anyone else with comments, questions, or objections to this file?

lines.speaker: Resident 14
lines.label: Resident 14
lines.text: Hi, I'm, I'm, uh, I'm, uh, [Resident 14] at 121, uh, Lumber. As you can see, the whole neighborhood has basically came out in support that we did not approve of this. Thank you. I don't know on how many times you have stuff come here that where you have such a turnout from the local neighborhood against something, but it just shows you on how tight we are, that we do value our— what we believe is true. And we just hope this would stay that way.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. In answer to your question, [Resident 14], that yes, occasionally there are larger groups that come, neighborhoods like yourself that have a real tight sense of community and belonging, and yeah, then they fight for what they want. And so yeah, it— Thank you. It does happen. Is there anyone else with comments, questions, or objections? I'll ask one more time. Is there anyone else with comments, questions, or objections to this file? Then I will close the public hearing, open the council meeting. Thank you. Council, how would you like to proceed? Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I'll make a motion to deny.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Penner. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Uh, thank you, Mr. Mayor. Uh, typically with, uh, rezoning applications like this, it's a tricky balancing act. Uh, this one is not particularly difficult, uh, for a number of reasons. Uh, public hearings do matter. It actually does make a difference when people come to these hearings. So anyone who ever has the impression or thought that, uh, public hearings don't make a difference, they do. And because we do want to hear what neighbours have to say. I agree with many of the concerns in regards to the substantial change to the neighbourhood in terms of the— just the number of units that are being proposed. I would have concerns on that. And I think the message is also very clear that if you're looking to develop in an established neighbourhood, it would be wise to consult with neighbours, with the neighbourhood prior to coming to a public hearing. That's what— Thank you. Normally has happened in the past. Where it has the— where there's a development that could be contentious is that the developer would meet with neighbours in advance. And I'm just not impressed by presentations that spitball pools and gardens and golf simulators and all that. We need actual plans and consultation should happen prior to this process rather than having it short-circuited halfway through with a suggestion to table and all that, because that doesn't— Thank you. is not how the neighbourhood should be treated in this regard. So it's a very clear denial, and I'm quite comfortable with that.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Well, this is very easy. When the applicant themselves requests the denial of an application, then I will be one to oblige. I will say that this is kind of— this is leapfrogging. This isn't in the transitional zone in our official community plan that ends at Second Street. There will always be challenges when development does come. There will be always that first building that does begin to change a neighborhood, but our transition zone is at Second Street right now and not at Third Street. So I would advise to the applicants, if you are trying to do that, hopefully they—

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: You heard some common themes here of how you could show some faith of goodwill to the community and then go from there.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further, council? Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I agree with the comments made, especially the leapfrogging on our community plan. I think that is part of it too. On the other hand, we have developers in Steinbach who buy up lots to do different development in different areas, and one of the problems we have in our downtown core is the large lots, large, deep, narrow lots, and there's not a whole lot of options. And if they're choosing not to build Or it's not affordable to build single-family homes on those large lots, then what do they do? Like, what are the plans, right? So they need to maybe cobble together a couple lots or whatever the situation. I'm not a developer, I wouldn't know. But I know we've run into this a number of times with these long, deep lots is what goes on them, and the neighbourhood certainly needs to be involved. I appreciate all the comments and the passion for your It's a microcommunity within Steinbach. We have lots of those. And while, like I said, it's not necessarily practical to build a single-family home, what is practical on there— and I agree, a 3-storey would be too much, but what is acceptable. But we'll let the developer work on that, and then maybe the next time he comes back here, we'll have a different reaction.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Go ahead, Councillor Pincott.

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. My decision is based on respect for the community. I think the community has spoken and we've heard, and hopefully if a new plan does come up in the future, it will be a plan that the community can agree with. That's my comment. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything in closing? Well, council, Yes, this is, this is an easy decision, and I want to thank the, the, the neighborhood, every one of you, for coming out. And I do— it wasn't too many years ago, a couple years ago, we moved off of 195 Lumber, and I understand what you say by that community. Uh, it was just, it was such a loving community. Someone wasn't feeling good, they got muffins. Um, I was the guy with the I had a snowblower, so everyone's driveway was clear on that section. Thank you. You know, [Resident 6], [Resident 6], I can totally appreciate what you talk about. That's just a different kind of neighborhood, and I respect very much what you've done. I thought for ease and simplicity, we could close the meeting, I did not want to disrespect you, and I do want to respect— I wanted— I'm glad we got to hear everyone's comments because it made a difference for all of us. And thank you. Go back to your neighborhood and keep loving each other and keep doing the good things, because I will support this motion as well. Okay, call for the question. All those in favor of Opposed? That is carried. Okay, council, we'll go to 6D. This is, uh, conditional use CU-202301 referring to 39 Keating Road. Second. At this time, I will— We'll wait.

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Things calm down a little bit.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. At this time, we will— I'll close the meeting. I will close the council meeting, open the public hearing. Mr. Warkentin, could you please introduce this file?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Yes, Mr. Mayor, members of council. This public hearing and application relates to conditional use file CU-2023-01 for property with civic address of 39 Keating Road. The applicant for the conditional use is Graham Pollock. The owners of the property are Steinbach and Area Animal Rescue This is an application by [name withheld]. Purpose of the conditional use application is to allow an RTM, ready-to-move structure to be placed onto the subject property for the purpose of being used as an animal shelter. Pursuant to city zoning bylaw 2100, any building moved within the city does require a conditional use approval. Notices as required under the Planning Act have been issued. There is no written correspondence on the file. Recommendation from administration is for council to approve conditional use subject to information that may be presented at the hearing and subject to an easement agreement for utilities along fronting the property.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Warkentin. Is the applicant here today? Do you wish to speak? Uh, I don't— might as well, uh, give us the presentation now.

lines.speaker: Graham Pollock
lines.title: Vice President
lines.label: Graham Pollock (Vice President, Steinbach & Area Animal Rescue)
lines.text: Um, hi, my name is Graham Pawlik. I'm the vice president of the Steinbach and Area Animal Rescue. I live at 92 Meadowlark Lane in the RM of La Broquerie. With me is our rescue president, Michelle Neufeld. This is, uh, thank you for allowing us the time to, to speak to you and, um, present on, on our application to move an RTM onto our property. We've owned the property for, I would say, 5 years, I think 5 or 6 years roughly, and this is kind of the culmination of, of our goal of what it's always been is to build an animal rescue within the city of Steinbach to serve Steinbach and the community and the surrounding communities. We've taken a great deal of effort in this plan, and I believe you've got the artist rendering as well as the floor plan. We've taken a great deal of thought and plan into keeping the outside The facade of the building to look like a residence. It in fact is a 1,600-square-foot residence that we've custom redesigned the floor plan for. So we do have residences on the west side of Keating Road, and, and we wanted to maintain that integrity and not build kind of a factory-type building as opposed to a residence. Thank you. type building. So driving by this building on Keating Road, you would never know it was an animal rescue other than for the sign outside and probably the parking lot. We were really concerned about that part of it to kind of maintain that community integrity. But this has been a long time coming for us. We've worked very hard for this. Thank you. The nice thing for us is, is the builder of our RTM is Mark's RTM. He is located 7.5 miles straight north of our property on Keating Road. So the move of the building would not come within the City of Steinbach limits other than moving onto our property. It would stay on Keating Road all the way from his property straight south to where we reside. Where our property is. The only highway that he would be crossing on the move is 311, and obviously all the highway permits and moving permits would be done by the moving company in advance. But it's a simple move. It's not coming down any highways or any residential streets within the city of Steinbach, and for that reason, It makes it a fairly easy thing for us to do. So other than answering questions for you, I don't really have a whole lot to offer. I think that it's a great plan. It's going to serve this community in ways that we can't even begin to think. And I think that it's been a very long time coming for us. Thank you. and we're ready to proceed, so.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, any questions of council? Go ahead, Councillor Siemens, and then Councillor Pincott.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you. I like the concept. I like the idea. You're right. I think it was about 6 years ago you were before council when you bought the property, and there was a few concerns from the residents of loud dogs, a lot of traffic at night. Have you addressed— you're able to address all those?

lines.speaker: Graham Pollock
lines.title: Vice President
lines.label: Graham Pollock (Vice President, Steinbach & Area Animal Rescue)
lines.text: Well, dogs wouldn't be outside if we did have any dogs. First of all, this is the— we can't consider this to be like a Humane Society where animals will come and stay long-term. We're— we still need our fosters. We still are a foster-based rescue. And the idea of this is is going to allow us to take animals in need that urgently need to come in and have a place to house them for 2 days, 3 days, a week until we can move them to a good match for a foster home. So long-term stays are not something we want to do with this. With respect to dogs, and dogs barking. Neighbors have dogs and they bark too. So the dogs would not be outside at night. They would be inside. If we did have more than one in at any given time, then yeah, they would be obviously inside. And hopefully the soundproofing in the place is good enough that you're not going to hear the dog barking. And Outside across the road. But, but yeah, so it really is— it's not designed to be a humane society. It's designed to be a shelter where we can deal with animals. For example, a mom cat and 6 kittens that are found on the side of the road, we can bring them in right away, we can quarantine them, we can deal with them vetting-wise, and then get them off to a foster home as soon as we've got a foster available. Thank you. And that's the whole idea of it.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: So good, thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Go ahead, Councillor.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Question to administration.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you. Through you, Mr. Warkentin, as this is pertaining to a conditional use for an RTM, I'm just wondering what the— if you have any insight as to why the city does not allow or requires a conditional use for RTMs and they're just not greenlit automatically.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Mr. Mayor. City zoning bylaw does speak to any building moved into the city, not just RTMs. It is rare, but Mr. Pawlik did allude to it briefly in his comments. It sometimes can be a challenge when moving buildings down public streets. There have been more instances of buildings moved out of Steinbach than Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is a very unique application. It's the first time that a structure has been moved in. As mentioned in my background report to council, there is only one other precedent in the city's history, at least for my history with the city over the past 30 years, where a structure has been permitted to be moved into the city. There's ample opportunity for buildings and structures to be built on site without having the need to move these structures. structures down public roads, and that's the prime consideration.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: So just a follow-up question. Go ahead. So primarily it's not due to building spec or anything like that, it's mainly just due to the transportation logistics of it?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Well, that's part of it. In this case, it is a brand new structure. There have been instances where existing buildings have been moved within the City of Steinbach from one neighborhood to the other. For example, Homes with particular character heritage and of sufficient structural integrity that they're able to be moved. The other factor is, again, because it's conditional use, it's a matter of council's view as to whether or not neighborhoods would be negatively impacted. And in many cases, when there are buildings being moved, Yes. More often than not, it's existing buildings that may be quite old. And with those applications, if older buildings are permitted to move into newer neighborhoods, that can have significant impacts on, on neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you. Anything further? Okay, I guess you can take your seat. Is there anyone here with comments, questions, or objections to this file? I'll ask one more time. Is there anyone here with comments, questions, or objections to this file? Okay, seeing none, I will close the public hearing, open the council meeting. Council, how would you like to proceed?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Alderman Siemens, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: I am very pleased to be moving this motion. I— this is long overdue for our community. Mr. Pawlik mentioned that this is really long overdue, and what I really appreciate about this is how thoughtful it is. The whole organization I have found to be well-run and efficient with the resources they have, and I think this new facility is another example of that. It's, it's really a creative, um, it's a creative option, I would say, and really thoughtful, even taking into consideration the, the street they're on and, you know, what's happening in that street with there being residential houses a little bit further down. But I just, for one, I'm very thankful for the work the organization does. I'm very happy to see this moving forward.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing further.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further, council? Anything in closing? Well, I too am very glad this is happening. One of the— one of the— I don't know, you're probably still a volunteer, Michelle. You've done this out of your house for so many years and now you finally have— you're going to have a brand new wonderful place to take care of pets. That are either abandoned or lost or whatever, but you'll be rehoming them. And this is so exciting. And we are— I think there's a few pet lovers around the table here, and we think that this is a great thing. You've done it well, and you've got the notice of our provincial government as well. And I think that is the right thing to do. Thank you. It's to grant this conditional use and, and get you guys up and running as quick as we can. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Thank you. Okay, council, there are no delegations, no reports and recommendations. We've taken care of administration. We'll go to council question period. Are there any questions of council? Okay, seeing none, we've got 11A, correspondence and petitions. Minister of Environment and Climate merit-based grant program. How would you like to proceed? Take his information? Okay. We have no other business. Looking for a motion to adjourn. Councillor Penner, seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Next regular council meeting is Tuesday, August 15th.
